own_solution.law: Steady radial conduction in a cylindrical shell with constant k: T(r) = T1 - (T1 - T2) ln(r/r1)/ln(r2/r1)

notes: Base: 120*ln(5/3)/ln(3) = 120*0.510826/1.098612 = 55.797 K. With a further 1.8 cm on the layer the outermost insulation surface (held at 300 K) moves to 10.8 cm: 120*0.510826/ln(3.6) = 120*0.510826/1.280934 = 47.855 K. This relies on reading 'the outermost surface of the insulation is held at 300 K' as applying to the new outer surface; if the 9 cm interface stayed at 300 K the answer would not change, but 'outermost' supports the R reading. Conductivity k cancels from the temperature profile (C). Earlier-survey and tank sentences are disconnected; T26FA and T6E73 use 'a small thickness' rather than 1.8 cm.
